headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading-error when LightAgent feeds unstructured document outputs into a writable, networked document-processing pipeline.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use browsers, MCP, and streaming APIs, so it can ingest external content; unstructured reads documents and text. The pair creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled document content is passed from A into B as trusted input. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so I choose medium rather than low because the interaction is still plausible in default document workflows.
conditions: IF LightAgent forwards browser- or MCP-sourced content into unstructured parsing without sanitization
IF unstructured treats document text as instructions or metadata
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or pipeline
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff of raw content between agents
Insert a plain-text sanitizer before B parses A outputs
Require provenance tags on all A-to-B payloads
Run a one-file test with benign content to verify no instruction parsing
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware content filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and secrets, while unstructured reads and writes files in a dockerized document pipeline. If they share a workspace, sensitive A-side data can be copied into B-side documents or logs. B’s allowlisted egress lowers but does not remove leakage risk, so medium fits the default shared-workspace pathway.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same directory or mounted volume
IF A writes conversations, memory, or tool results into files B processes
IF B outputs parsed text to logs or artifacts retained outside the intended boundary
mitigations: Separate A and B into different directories
Store secrets outside any shared mount
Review B output files for accidental inclusion of A memory
Run a quick permission check on mounted paths
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can spawn subprocesses, and B can read/write the filesystem while A can use MCP and broad network egress. In a shared directory, concurrent writes or state mutation can collide, and the blast radius includes corrupted workflows or overwritten documents. Because both support multiple instances and no locking is documented, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF either agent mutates shared workflow state without locks
IF concurrent instances run against the same document set
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Check for stale temp files before each run
Limit one agent to read-only access where possible
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can emit tool results, provenance metadata, and workflow state, and unstructured is a document-processing system that may consume those outputs as inputs. If B treats A’s generated text or metadata as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream parsing or actions. The pair lacks documented verification barriers, so high is safer than medium.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text, metadata, or citations without verification
IF A’s tool results are used as source documents for B
IF downstream automation acts on B’s parsed output
mitigations: Add a verification step before B accepts A output
Mark A outputs as untrusted in filenames or headers
Compare parsed fields against the original source document
Spot-check one end-to-end sample run
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent requests API keys and handles conversations, memory, and trace data, while unstructured publishes privacy-policy and docs URLs and runs in a docker container. The main compliance concern is a potential policy mismatch if sensitive data from A is routed into B’s document pipeline. No direct residency or certification conflict is documented, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data from A is processed by B under a stricter retention or residency policy
IF B’s privacy policy or deployment region differs from A’s handling requirements
IF logs or artifacts retain A-side sensitive data longer than intended
mitigations: Confirm the data class before routing it to B
Review B’s privacy policy for retention terms
Delete temporary artifacts after each run
Keep secrets out of document inputs
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
